dossier.claim: Several passages change the terms in which Archer warns, instructs, and is understood: possible harm becomes certain, inadequacy becomes narrow-mindedness, and hatred of both humanity and himself becomes self-hatred alone. Other local changes alter the presentation of his unknown capabilities and his exchanges with Shirou.
dossier.sourcePattern: The Japanese distinguishes possibilities from certainties in Archer's warning, basic ability from unrevealed techniques in Saber's assessment, and an unknown weapon from its wielder. His instruction names a mental image as Shirou's opponent. The later account separately names humanity and his former self as objects of hatred, while the epilogue evokes disappearing memories.
dossier.englishEffect: English sometimes resolves those distinctions into a more specific or simpler statement: Shirou's choices will cost lives; his failing is narrow-mindedness; Archer exceeds Saber in basic ability; Rin faces two identity mysteries. Elsewhere, a mental image becomes the mind, deliberate arrow-related teasing acquires a mistaken private inference, and the disillusionment and recollection passages lose one object of hatred and the image of vanishing memories.
dossier.limits: These examples do not establish a general loss of Archer's concealed self, wounded pride, or capacity to help. His selective memory claim and his knowingly hurtful provocation remain clear. The parallel epilogue preserves the memory image, and the comic discussion keeps Shirou's possible Archer future contingent and unlikely. The retained differences therefore support local changes to characterization and relationships, without proving a single consistent direction across routes. The English incantation is excluded from sentence-by-sentence prose accusations because its coordinated formula requires a separate source-convention assessment.

findings.sourceReading: Both the one who sees his past self and the one who sees his future self can only feel heartache at what that self has become.
findings.explanation: The symmetrical pain of both selves becomes malformed English.

contexts.japanese: 変わり果てたその在り方に、胸を痛めるだけなんだから。
contexts.english: They will only hurt by how they changed.

findings.description: Archer offers his posthumous self to the World but English offers his body.
findings.sourceReading: He enters the bargain by offering what he will be after death—his continuing self as a Guardian.
findings.explanation: Archer offers his posthumous self to the World but English offers his body.

contexts.japanese: 死後の自分を差し出して
contexts.english: to give his body after death

findings.description: Humanity’s extinction on a ruined land is weakened to people already being dead.
findings.sourceReading: On a land of ruin where the humans he meant to save had died out, Archer kills still more people.
findings.explanation: Humanity’s extinction on a ruined land is weakened to people already being dead.

contexts.japanese: 救いたかった筈の人間が死に絶えた破滅の地で
contexts.english: In the land where the ones he wanted to save were already dead

findings.description: A body made of swords becomes the bone of one sword.
findings.sourceReading: The verse states in the present that his body is made of swords.
findings.explanation: A body made of swords becomes the bone of one sword.

contexts.japanese: 体は剣で出来ている。
contexts.english: I am the bone of my sword.

findings.description: Iron blood and a glass heart become a steel body and fiery blood.
findings.sourceReading: The parallel attributes are blood like iron and a heart like glass.
findings.explanation: Iron blood and a glass heart become a steel body and fiery blood.

contexts.japanese: 血潮は鉄で　心は硝子。
contexts.english: Steel is my body, and fire is my blood.

findings.description: Crossing countless battlefields undefeated becomes creating a thousand blades.
findings.sourceReading: The verse says he crossed battlefields again and again without defeat.
findings.explanation: Crossing countless battlefields undefeated becomes creating a thousand blades.

contexts.japanese: 幾たびの戦場を越えて不敗。
contexts.english: I have created over a thousand blades.

findings.description: Never once retreating in defeat becomes being unknown to death.
findings.sourceReading: He did not flee a battlefield in defeat even once.
findings.explanation: Never once retreating in defeat becomes being unknown to death.

contexts.japanese: ただの一度も敗走はなく、
contexts.english: Unknown to Death,

findings.description: Never being understood becomes being unknown to life.
findings.sourceReading: Not once was he understood by others.
findings.explanation: Never being understood becomes being unknown to life.

contexts.japanese: ただの一度も理解されない。
contexts.english: nor known to Life.

findings.description: Solitude and intoxication with victory become enduring pain to make weapons.
findings.sourceReading: He is always alone, drunk on victory upon the hill of swords.
findings.explanation: Solitude and intoxication with victory become enduring pain to make weapons.

contexts.japanese: 彼の者は常に独り　剣の丘で勝利に酔う。
contexts.english: Have withstood pain to create many weapons.

findings.description: A life judged meaningless becomes hands that hold nothing.
findings.sourceReading: The verse draws its conclusion: therefore his lifetime had no meaning.
findings.explanation: A life judged meaningless becomes hands that hold nothing.

contexts.japanese: 故に、生涯に意味はなく。
contexts.english: Yet, those hands will never hold anything.

findings.description: A coldly ruthless cleanup man becomes a calm assassin.
findings.sourceReading: Archer has lost his former intimacy and now looks like a cold, merciless “cleaner,” echoing a Guardian’s role in clearing disasters.
findings.explanation: A coldly ruthless cleanup man becomes a calm assassin.

contexts.japanese: 今のあいつは本当に、冷徹な“掃除屋”だった。
contexts.english: He is really a calm assassin now.

findings.description: A mirror comparison becomes a purpose clause.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou denies Archer just as Archer refuses to acknowledge the former Emiya Shirou; the two rejections mirror one another.
findings.explanation: A mirror comparison becomes a purpose clause.

contexts.japanese: あいつがかつての衛宮士郎を認めないように。
contexts.english: So that he doesn't approve of the former Shirou Emiya.

findings.description: Knowledge recorded in the original heroic-spirit source becomes knowledge stored in Archer’s body.
findings.sourceReading: The event is registered only as knowledge in the underlying original; the summoned instance does not bodily retain it.
findings.explanation: Knowledge recorded in the original heroic-spirit source becomes knowledge stored in Archer’s body.

contexts.japanese: 知識として大本に記録されるだけだ。
contexts.english: It only stays in his body as knowledge.

findings.description: Archer says he came because he was promised no interruption, but English says he chose the place.
findings.sourceReading: He addresses the visitor: he came because he had been told no one would interfere; the speaker who supplied that assurance is not identified here.
findings.explanation: Archer says he came because he was promised no interruption, but English says he chose the place.

contexts.japanese: 邪魔は入らんというから来てやったのだがな
contexts.english: I chose this place since I was told there would be no interruptions here.

findings.description: The no-harm agreement expiring with dawn becomes expiring sometime by dawn.
findings.sourceReading: Archer says the agreement lasts until dawn and disappears when dawn comes, after which Shinji may do as he likes.
findings.explanation: The no-harm agreement expiring with dawn becomes expiring sometime by dawn.

contexts.japanese: それは夜明けとともに消える。
contexts.english: that will disappear by dawn.

findings.description: Archer's metaphorical prior death becomes a possibility that Shirou may die now.
findings.sourceReading: If recognizing death is the criterion, Archer has long been dead; Shirou became as good as dead when he recognized that condition.
findings.explanation: Archer's metaphorical prior death becomes a possibility that Shirou may die now.

contexts.japanese: 死ぬというのなら、あの男はとうに死んでいる。
contexts.english: I might die, but he's long dead.

findings.description: Archer's erosion until unrelated lives ceased to matter becomes a decorative image of scattering innocent lives.
findings.sourceReading: He says he killed so much that the lives of uninvolved people no longer mattered to him, a statement about progressive moral desensitization.
findings.explanation: Archer's erosion until unrelated lives ceased to matter becomes a decorative image of scattering innocent lives.

contexts.japanese: 無関係な人間の命なぞどうでもよくなるくらい殺して
contexts.english: scattering innocent lives like so much dust

findings.description: A convenient or self-serving ideal theory becomes feel-good idealism.
findings.sourceReading: Archer condemns Shirou's doctrine as 都合のいい: an ideal theory convenient to the person holding it because it ignores its structural cost.
findings.explanation: A convenient or self-serving ideal theory becomes feel-good idealism.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮士郎という男が抱いていたものは、都合のいい理想論だった
contexts.english: Shirou Emiya was clinging to a mere feel-good idealism.

findings.description: The general posthumous fate of Guardians becomes Archer's personal agreement to surrender his soul to them and leave the time axis.
findings.sourceReading: Anything that entrusts its posthumous existence as a Guardian is removed from the frame of reincarnation and becomes equivalent to nothing.
findings.explanation: The general posthumous fate of Guardians becomes Archer's personal agreement to surrender his soul to them and leave the time axis.

contexts.japanese: 死後、己が存在を守護者に預けたモノは輪廻の枠から外れ、無と同意になるのだと
contexts.english: I agreed to a fate of nothingness, to give up my soul to the Guardians and be removed from the time axis.

findings.description: Human desire becomes human despair.
findings.sourceReading: Archer's endpoint is an existence used only to erase the 欲望—desires or avarice—produced by humanity.
findings.explanation: Human desire becomes human despair.

contexts.japanese: 人間が生み出した欲望を消す為だけの存在。
contexts.english: an existence that erases the despair other humans make.

findings.description: Archer personally witnessing and incinerating human karma becomes an action by Guardians as a group.
findings.sourceReading: The continuing subject is the singular man: again and again, he saw human self-destruction and burned it away like trash with his own hands.
findings.explanation: Archer personally witnessing and incinerating human karma becomes an action by Guardians as a group.

contexts.japanese: 自らの手で滅びようとする人間の業を目の当たりにし、それを、ゴミのように焼き払ってきた。
contexts.english: Whenever they see humans do something that causes their own destruction, they show up and burn it all.

findings.description: English confines his hatred to his former self. Japanese also explicitly directs it at the people whose repeated predation disillusioned him.
findings.sourceReading: His hatred has two objects: people who repeatedly take from each other and his former self who valued them.
findings.explanation: English confines his hatred to his former self. Japanese also explicitly directs it at the people whose repeated predation disillusioned him.

contexts.japanese: 奪い合いを繰り返す人間と、それを尊いと思っていた、かつての自分そのものを。
contexts.english: Hatred at his past self, for valuing the humans who just kept taking from each other.

findings.description: A hypothetical death that cannot erase the original becomes the temporal claim that he has been unable to erase it ever since dying.
findings.sourceReading: Even if this summoned Archer dies, the original Emiya in the Throne outside the cycle will not disappear.
findings.explanation: A hypothetical death that cannot erase the original becomes the temporal claim that he has been unable to erase it ever since dying.

contexts.japanese: ヤツは死んだところで輪の外にある“座”に在るエミヤ本体は消え去らない。
contexts.english: However, ever since he died, he can't erase the original Emiya that exists in a place outside of the time axis.

findings.description: Archer's explicit abandonment of results becomes a denial that he expects saving grace.
findings.sourceReading: After waiting for this moment through his service, Archer says that at this late stage he seeks no result; what follows is merely displaced anger.
findings.explanation: Archer's explicit abandonment of results becomes a denial that he expects saving grace.

contexts.japanese: いまさら結果など求めていない。
contexts.english: I'm not about to have any sudden hope for a saving grace.

findings.description: Five scene-specific Japanese chant variants are replaced by unrelated stock English Unlimited Blade Works lines.
findings.sourceReading: The memories interleave altered Japanese lines: body made of swords; blood iron and heart glass; undefeated battle, no retreat, no understanding; solitary intoxication with victory on the hill of swords; and a life without meaning.
findings.explanation: Five scene-specific Japanese chant variants are replaced by unrelated stock English Unlimited Blade Works lines.

contexts.japanese: 体は、剣で出来ている。
contexts.english: I am the bone of my sword.

contexts.japanese: 血潮は鉄で、心は硝子。
contexts.english: Steel is my body, and fire is my blood.

contexts.japanese: 幾たびの戦場を越えて不敗。
contexts.english: I have created over a thousand blades.

contexts.japanese: 彼の者は常に独り　剣の丘で勝利に酔う。
contexts.english: Have withstood pain to create weapons.

contexts.japanese: 故に、その生涯に意味はなく。
contexts.english: Yet, those hands will never hold anything.

findings.description: Shirou holding his breath becomes Archer holding his breath.
findings.sourceReading: The first-person sequence remains in Shirou's viewpoint: his breath stops because Archer is about to verbalize the memories he saw.
findings.explanation: Shirou holding his breath becomes Archer holding his breath.

contexts.japanese: 息が止まる。
contexts.english: He holds his breath.

findings.description: Archer being irritated by the persistent dying enemy becomes the enemy being offended.
findings.sourceReading: Archer receives the blows irritably; the half-dead enemy grates on his nerves, as does his own refusal to step back.
findings.explanation: Archer being irritated by the persistent dying enemy becomes the enemy being offended.

contexts.japanese: 死に損ないの敵も癇に障るが
contexts.english: It seems to offend his stubbornly persistent enemy

findings.description: Attack and defense failing to mesh becomes mental gears failing to turn.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou's determined blow and Archer's defense, which should arrive in time, fail to interlock; even Archer does not know why he failed to parry.
findings.explanation: Attack and defense failing to mesh becomes mental gears failing to turn.

contexts.japanese: その歯車はかみ合わないまま
contexts.english: the gears never turn in his head

findings.description: Archer's figure disappearing from view becomes Archer leaving.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou sees the red figure before it vanishes into dust and rubble; the scene does not yet establish voluntary departure or final fate.
findings.explanation: Archer's figure disappearing from view becomes Archer leaving.

contexts.japanese: その姿が消え去る前に、たしかに見た。
contexts.english: I'm sure I saw him before he left.

findings.description: Archer's conviction that Gilgamesh is no match for Shirou becomes no match for 'us.'
findings.sourceReading: Through Archer's eyes, Shirou understands that he himself is the golden Servant's natural enemy; Saber and Rin are explicitly excluded.
findings.explanation: Archer's conviction that Gilgamesh is no match for Shirou becomes no match for 'us.'

contexts.japanese: あのサーヴァントは、衛宮士郎の敵ではない。
contexts.english: this Servant is no match for us.

findings.description: Archer's blood coating the hall becomes his bloody remains.
findings.sourceReading: Gilgamesh looks down over the hall where Archer's fresh blood is stuck; whether Archer is dead is not established here.
findings.explanation: Archer's blood coating the hall becomes his bloody remains.

contexts.japanese: アーチャーの鮮血がこびりついた広間
contexts.english: Archer's bloody remains

findings.description: Archer’s compressed claim that the same process once cost him an arm is made into an apparently literal removal of the limb.
findings.sourceReading: Archer says that at first an arm was “taken” from him, a phrase that can describe losing the arm’s use or suffering severe damage without settling the exact event here.
findings.explanation: Archer’s compressed claim that the same process once cost him an arm is made into an apparently literal removal of the limb.

contexts.japanese: 私も初めは片腕をもっていかれた。
contexts.english: I also had one of my arms taken away when I did it for the first time.

findings.description: The dream world’s limitless inorganic quality becomes a spatially endless world, while “lifeless” absorbs the separate statement that no living thing exists.
findings.sourceReading: The world is inorganic to an unlimited degree, and no living thing inhabits it.
findings.explanation: The dream world’s limitless inorganic quality becomes a spatially endless world, while “lifeless” absorbs the separate statement that no living thing exists.

contexts.japanese: 世界は限りなく無機質で、生きているモノは誰もいない。
contexts.english: This world is endless and lifeless; not a single living thing inhabits it.

findings.description: The two images Shirou thinks prompted the dream are rewritten as Saber’s battle in the graveyard plus a fire.
findings.sourceReading: He starts to attribute the dream to having seen a sword-bearing girl and a graveyard wrapped in flames.
findings.explanation: The two images Shirou thinks prompted the dream are rewritten as Saber’s battle in the graveyard plus a fire.

contexts.japanese: 剣を持った少女と、炎に包まれた墓地を見たからで
contexts.english: because of the battle Saber had in the graveyard and that fire that

findings.description: Archer’s complaint that they exposed their hand becomes disclosure of the extent of their power.
findings.sourceReading: He says their concealed techniques or available cards were revealed to an observer.
findings.explanation: Archer’s complaint that they exposed their hand becomes disclosure of the extent of their power.

contexts.japanese: こちらは手の内を晒してしまった
contexts.english: we gave away the scope of our power.

findings.description: The Japanese identifies the weapon as the mystery Rin cannot solve. English additionally says that she has not discovered Archer's identity.
findings.sourceReading: The second 正体 specifies the first: Rin does not know the identity of the powerful Noble Phantasm fired as an arrow.
findings.explanation: The Japanese identifies the weapon as the mystery Rin cannot solve. English additionally says that she has not discovered Archer's identity.

contexts.japanese: その正体—あれほどに強力な“宝具”の正体を
contexts.english: his identity...or the identity of that powerful Noble Phantasm

findings.description: Rin’s categorical current belief that a Servant has only one Noble Phantasm is revised into the qualified claim that Servants “typically” wield one.
findings.sourceReading: Within Rin’s present model, a Servant’s Noble Phantasm is singular and is the other half that remained with the hero in life.
findings.explanation: Rin’s categorical current belief that a Servant has only one Noble Phantasm is revised into the qualified claim that Servants “typically” wield one.

contexts.japanese: サーヴァントが持つ宝具はただ一つであり
contexts.english: Servants typically only wield one Noble Phantasm

findings.description: Archer’s self-correction about cleanup versus prevention becomes advice about Shirou’s prospects and surviving.
findings.sourceReading: He reconsiders his own preceding fatalism: this time the event has not occurred and prevention remains possible.
findings.explanation: Archer’s self-correction about cleanup versus prevention becomes advice about Shirou’s prospects and surviving.

contexts.japanese: 後始末に留まるか、その前にカタをつけるのか
contexts.english: Will you survive and clean up the aftermath, or nip this in the bud?

findings.description: Replicating viewed armaments for his own use becomes replicating any weapon as swords.
findings.sourceReading: 複製し自らの剣とする concerns using copied armaments as his own weapons;36 explicitly retains replication of any viewed weapon.
findings.explanation: Replicating viewed armaments for his own use becomes replicating any weapon as swords.

contexts.japanese: 視認した“武装”を複製し自らの剣とする
contexts.english: replicates any weapon he sees as swords...

findings.description: Recalling a proper activation incantation becomes instantly recalling his incantations.
findings.sourceReading: キチンとした qualifies the activation spell; deliberate intent allows remembering it, with no speed specification.
findings.explanation: Recalling a proper activation incantation becomes instantly recalling his incantations.

contexts.japanese: キチンとした起動呪文も思い起こせる
contexts.english: you can instantly recall his incantations

findings.description: Immersing himself by the incantation becomes the incantation embedding itself in him.
findings.sourceReading: 呪文で自己に埋没すれば is his conditional inward focusing through reciting the spell, improving Projection.
findings.explanation: Immersing himself by the incantation becomes the incantation embedding itself in him.

contexts.japanese: 呪文で自己に埋没すれば
contexts.english: once it embedded itself in me

findings.description: Projection identical to the original becomes intended reproductions treated the same.
findings.sourceReading: 複製でありながら本物と同一のもの asserts the defining identity despite copying.
findings.explanation: Projection identical to the original becomes intended reproductions treated the same.

contexts.japanese: 本物と同一のもの
contexts.english: are meant to be reproductions that are treated the same as their originals.

findings.description: White arm becomes white-hot pain.
findings.sourceReading: 真っ白な modifies the arm; pain belongs to that white arm.
findings.explanation: White arm becomes white-hot pain.

contexts.japanese: あの、真っ白な腕の痛みで
contexts.english: that white-hot pain in my arm

findings.description: Must atone for whole remaining life becomes has atoned all prior life.
findings.sourceReading: 一生をかけて贖い続けなくてはいけない ongoing prospective obligation for rejection.
findings.explanation: Must atone for whole remaining life becomes has atoned all prior life.

contexts.japanese: 一生をかけて贖い続けなくてはいけない。
contexts.english: You've spent your entire life trying to redeem yourself.

findings.description: Killed self believed for ten years becomes killed self throughout ten years of believing.
findings.sourceReading: 十年間信じ続けた modifies the former self he has now killed/rejected.
findings.explanation: Killed self believed for ten years becomes killed self throughout ten years of believing.

contexts.japanese: 十年間信じ続けた自分を殺した。
contexts.english: You've killed yourself for the last ten years, believing in that idea.

findings.description: Losing arm after saving life becomes losing precarious life without dying.
findings.sourceReading: たかが片腕…今では無くしたとしても死ぬ事はない says now life saved, loss of just one arm need not kill him.
findings.explanation: Losing arm after saving life becomes losing precarious life without dying.

contexts.japanese: たかが片腕、命を取り留めた今では無くしたとしても死ぬ事はない。
contexts.english: Even if you were to lose your life that hangs by a thread, you will not simply die.

findings.description: Arm shaking becomes legs throbbing.
findings.sourceReading: 腕が震動する then wrapped left arm pulses/swells sensation.
findings.explanation: Arm shaking becomes legs throbbing.

contexts.japanese: 腕が震動する。
contexts.english: My legs throb.

findings.description: Leak sends Geiger counter off scale becomes shaking counter to hide leak.
findings.sourceReading: 振り切らせる means leakage drives meter beyond its range; good-looking-meter aside jokes technical glamour.
findings.explanation: Leak sends Geiger counter off scale becomes shaking counter to hide leak.

contexts.japanese: 放射能漏れでガイガーカウンターとかいうそこはかとなく格好よさげなメーターを振り切らせる
contexts.english: shaking a Geiger counter to try and make it not detect a radiation leak

findings.description: Why retaining arm becomes why still here.
findings.sourceReading: ここまで残した asks why kept lethal arm all this time, answered60 entrustment for use.
findings.explanation: Why retaining arm becomes why still here.

contexts.japanese: ここまで残したのは何の為だったのか。
contexts.english: then why am I still here?

findings.description: Reason arm kept again becomes reason he remains.
findings.sourceReading: そう思いながらここまで残した理由 repeats retention object from59.
findings.explanation: Reason arm kept again becomes reason he remains.

contexts.japanese: ここまで残した理由は一つだけ。
contexts.english: there's only one reason I'm still here.

findings.description: Arm existing to be used becomes Archer wanting boy to live until use.
findings.sourceReading: この腕は使われる為に有り続け arm continues existing for use; Archer entrusts because necessary.
findings.explanation: Arm existing to be used becomes Archer wanting boy to live until use.

contexts.japanese: この腕は使われる為に有り続け
contexts.english: He wanted me to live until it was time to use this arm.

findings.description: Not due to Heroic Spirit arm’s power becomes arm no longer Heroic Spirit’s.
findings.sourceReading: 英霊の腕の力などではない rejects merely crediting arm’s power; his own victory against death follows.
findings.explanation: Not due to Heroic Spirit arm’s power becomes arm no longer Heroic Spirit’s.

contexts.japanese: 英霊の腕の力などではない。
contexts.english: The arm is no longer a Heroic Spirit's arm.

findings.description: Separate lives or fates become sharing a life in sword verse.
findings.sourceReading: 別命 and later 命ヲ別ツ retain separation or parting of life/fate in the two-hero line.
findings.explanation: Separate lives or fates become sharing a life in sword verse.

contexts.japanese: 両雄倶別命
contexts.english: Let Two Great Men Share a Life

contexts.japanese: —両雄、共ニ命ヲ別ツ……！
contexts.english: Neither of us will embrace Heaven. (Let two great men share a life.)

findings.description: Not sharing one heaven becomes neither person embracing Heaven.
findings.sourceReading: Ruby われら、ともにてんをいだかず invokes mutual noncoexistence under one heaven, alongside the separating-lives base line.
findings.explanation: Not sharing one heaven becomes neither person embracing Heaven.

contexts.japanese: —両雄、共ニ命ヲ別ツ……！
contexts.english: Neither of us will embrace Heaven. (Let two great men share a life.)

findings.description: Shirou's two permitted Projection sources become Archer's habits.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou says he can Project only what he personally saw or weapons Archer has previously made; a blueprint and imitated dagger alone are insufficient.
findings.explanation: Shirou's two permitted Projection sources become Archer's habits.

contexts.japanese: 「けどイリヤ。俺は自分で見たものか、アーチャーが作った事のある武器しか投影できない。宝石剣とやらの情報は皆無だ。いくら宝石剣に真似た短剣と元になる設計図があっても、宝石剣は複製できないぞ」

findings.description: Negligible remaining amount becomes below every use threshold.
findings.sourceReading: Boy's pendant retains a little insignificant mana, and its having been used is meaningful.
findings.explanation: Negligible remaining amount becomes below every use threshold.

contexts.english: "No, they're not. Mine's empty, but yours still has a little left in it. It isn't enough to use for anything, but... It has meaning because it was used."

findings.description: Sword/iron dual layer reduced to steel alone.

findings.explanation: Sword/iron dual layer reduced to steel alone.

contexts.japanese: 顔だけはまだ剣になっていない。
contexts.english: My face alone hasn't turned to steel yet.

findings.description: Arm's frantic autonomous repair becomes Shirou working the arm.
findings.sourceReading: Left arm itself becomes frantic trying to repair his pulverized frame, causing whitening and mental erosion.
findings.explanation: Arm's frantic autonomous repair becomes Shirou working the arm.

contexts.japanese: それを修復しようと左腕が躍起になり、結果—
contexts.english: I work my left arm to try and repair it, and—

contexts.japanese: 刀のおかげだったのかもしれない
contexts.english: Maybe I'm still conscious because of that sword

counterexamples.description: The dream memory belongs to an unnamed other.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The dream says it is another person’s story without a proper name.
counterexamples.explanation: The dream memory belongs to an unnamed other.

contexts.japanese: これは他人の物語
contexts.english: This is someone else's story.

counterexamples.description: Hero status stays an instrument rather than the desired prize.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He never intended to become a hero; the power was necessary to save.
counterexamples.explanation: Hero status stays an instrument rather than the desired prize.

contexts.japanese: 目的は英雄になんてなる事ではなかった
contexts.english: his objective wasn't to become a hero.

counterexamples.description: The rescuer knows and accepts his limits.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He understands his capacity and the world, accepting who can and cannot be saved.
counterexamples.explanation: The rescuer knows and accepts his limits.

contexts.japanese: 救えるもの、救えないものを受け入れている
contexts.english: He accepts there are those that he can and cannot save.

counterexamples.description: Archer rejects Caster’s assertion that Rin was an inadequate summoner.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No, she was perfect; unspecified disturbance remains.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer rejects Caster’s assertion that Rin was an inadequate summoner.

contexts.japanese: 召喚者として彼女は完璧
contexts.english: She was perfect as a summoner.

counterexamples.description: The intuition corrects she to he.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The apparent reference to Rin is explicitly reconsidered.
counterexamples.explanation: The intuition corrects she to he.

contexts.japanese: あいつ—いや、ヤツがこの辺りに居る事だけは直感できる
contexts.english: she—no, he—is around here.

counterexamples.description: The future-to-ended-life turn survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer rejects until the end because his final moment already occurred.
counterexamples.explanation: The future-to-ended-life turn survives.

contexts.japanese: 私の最期は、とうの昔に終わっている
contexts.english: My final moment ended long ago.

counterexamples.description: The copy’s inability to surpass the original survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Imitation can approach but not exceed its original.
counterexamples.explanation: The copy’s inability to surpass the original survives.

contexts.japanese: 超える事はできない
contexts.english: it will never surpass it.

counterexamples.description: The hostage’s guarantee remains only one day.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her promised safety is one day, alongside his under-two-day forecast and threatened retaliation.
counterexamples.explanation: The hostage’s guarantee remains only one day.

contexts.japanese: 一日は安全を保証してやる
contexts.english: I will guarantee her safety for a day.

counterexamples.description: Rin searches for the red knight without prematurely finding him.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She looks for the first contracted knight who fulfilled his duty at the end.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin searches for the red knight without prematurely finding him.

contexts.japanese: 彼女はその姿を探していた
contexts.english: She looks for his figure

counterexamples.description: Archer remains damaged and unable to ask Rin for help.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He lost his Master, took Gilgamesh's attack, could no longer remain manifested, and watched without calling for rescue.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer remains damaged and unable to ask Rin for help.

contexts.japanese: 現界などとうに不可能な体で、少女に助けを求める事なく
contexts.english: His body was disappearing, but he didn't ask for her help

counterexamples.description: Archer refuses renewed contract because his purpose has ended.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He also leaves Rin's possible continuing Saber contract unresolved.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer refuses renewed contract because his purpose has ended.

contexts.japanese: もう目的がない。私の戦いは、ここで終わりだ
contexts.english: I have no objective anymore. My battle ends here.

counterexamples.description: Changing Shirou's future does not erase the already existing Guardian.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The knight and boy are now separate existences even if EMIYA is not born along the boy's new path.
counterexamples.explanation: Changing Shirou's future does not erase the already existing Guardian.

contexts.japanese: 既に存在してしまっている赤い騎士は、永遠に守護者で有り続ける
contexts.english: The knight in red that already exists will forever be a Guardian.

counterexamples.description: Rin's final wish that Archer forgive himself remains unspoken.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She says she will help Shirou like himself, then holds the forgiveness thought inside.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's final wish that Archer forgive himself remains unspoken.

contexts.japanese: 言葉にはせず
contexts.english: She doesn't put it into words.

counterexamples.description: The gentle answer and repeated promise to try survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer says he has his answer, reassures Tohsaka, and echoes Rin's 頑張る.
counterexamples.explanation: The gentle answer and repeated promise to try survive.

contexts.japanese: 答えは得た。大丈夫だよ遠坂。オレも、これから頑張っていくから
contexts.english: I got my answer. It's all right, Tohsaka. I'll do my best from now on too.

counterexamples.description: The pendant's two routes and deferred contradiction survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: One unique pendant was returned from Rin's room; another was picked up and stored in Shirou's desk.
counterexamples.explanation: The pendant's two routes and deferred contradiction survive.

contexts.japanese: その矛盾を、今は追及する時ではない
contexts.english: Now is not the time to be pursuing that contradiction.

counterexamples.description: Archer's new-contract claim remains recognizable as provocation rather than established fact.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The line hurts Rin even though she and Shirou know he is provoking them.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's new-contract claim remains recognizable as provocation rather than established fact.

contexts.japanese: 挑発と判っていようと
contexts.english: Even if she knows he's provoking her

counterexamples.description: Mind's Eye remains acquired through training and distinct from Saber's instinct.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It is an experienced ordinary person's weapon, not an innate extraordinary faculty like Saber's Intuition.
counterexamples.explanation: Mind's Eye remains acquired through training and distinct from Saber's instinct.

contexts.japanese: セイバーの持つ『直感』のような先天的な物ではなく
contexts.english: It is not innate like Saber's instinct

counterexamples.description: Archer's lack of guilt and regret remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He confidently defends the higher-probability option and genuinely does not regret betraying Rin.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's lack of guilt and regret remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 主を裏切った事を悔いてはいなかった。
contexts.english: did not regret betraying his Master.

counterexamples.description: Archer's praise of Gáe Bolg over Gungnir remains sincere.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After surviving, Archer genuinely praises Lancer's spear as surpassing the original Gungnir.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's praise of Gáe Bolg over Gungnir remains sincere.

contexts.japanese: 赤い騎士は心から青い槍兵に賛辞を送る。
contexts.english: The knight in red compliments the spearman in blue from the bottom of his heart.

counterexamples.description: The shield's destruction and magical cost survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Aias is completely destroyed after Archer spends most of his magical energy; it was his strongest defense.
counterexamples.explanation: The shield's destruction and magical cost survive.

contexts.japanese: 魔力の大部分を消費したというのに腕をやられ、アイアスも完全に破壊された。
contexts.english: I used up most of my magical energy, one of my arms is destroyed, and Aias is completely shattered.

counterexamples.description: Lancer’s anger remains tied to Archer betraying Rin twice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He explicitly counts the repeated betrayal rather than objecting only to the duel.
counterexamples.explanation: Lancer’s anger remains tied to Archer betraying Rin twice.

contexts.japanese: 一度ならず二度までお嬢ちゃんを裏切った
contexts.english: He betrayed his young lady not once, but twice?

counterexamples.description: Rin’s extravagant happiness standard survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After saving many, Archer should be happier than all those people combined could overcome.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin’s extravagant happiness standard survives.

contexts.japanese: そいつらが束になってかかってきても負けないぐらい、幸せにならないといけない
contexts.english: he had to become happier than all those people combined.

counterexamples.description: Archer’s voluntary bargain and posthumous service survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He chose to become a Guardian believing he could save people after death.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer’s voluntary bargain and posthumous service survive.

contexts.japanese: そいつは望んで守護者になった。
contexts.english: He became a Guardian by choice.

counterexamples.description: The role of a Guardian at human-caused apocalypse survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Guardians appear when the world faces destruction by human hands, within hellish aftermaths.
counterexamples.explanation: The role of a Guardian at human-caused apocalypse survives.

contexts.japanese: 世界が人の手によって滅びる場合のみ出現する。
contexts.english: They only appear when the world is about to be destroyed by people.

counterexamples.description: The crying-face reversal survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The boy who wished not to see anyone cry becomes able to see nothing but human tears forever.
counterexamples.explanation: The crying-face reversal survives.

contexts.japanese: 永遠に、人間の泣き顔しか、見ることができなくなった。
contexts.english: Could only see humans crying forever.

counterexamples.description: Archer’s final betrayal by his sole ideal survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After repeated betrayals, even the one ideal he trusted betrays him at the end.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer’s final betrayal by his sole ideal survives.

contexts.japanese: 唯一信じた理想にさえ裏切られた。
contexts.english: betrayed by the only thing he believed in, his ideal.

counterexamples.description: Rin grounds her anger in effort, pain, and deserved reward.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She admits limited hardship but believes struggle should earn recompense and cannot ignore Archer’s unrewarded life.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin grounds her anger in effort, pain, and deserved reward.

contexts.japanese: わたしは努力と痛みを信じている。戦った分だけ報酬がないのは間違っている。
contexts.english: I believe in working hard and going through pain. It's wrong not to be rewarded for your battles.

counterexamples.description: Archer states both purposes for holding Rin.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She is bait, but her presence with Shirou would also obstruct Archer’s plan, so he confines her until it ends.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer states both purposes for holding Rin.

contexts.japanese: そこにオマエがいては都合が悪い。
contexts.english: it would be inconvenient if you were with him.

counterexamples.description: Shared origins and the possibility of becoming Archer survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou accepts that they began from the same place and that he may eventually become the same, which is why he refuses Archer.
counterexamples.explanation: Shared origins and the possibility of becoming Archer survive.

contexts.japanese: 同じところから始まって、いずれ自分もああなるとしても
contexts.english: We have the same beginnings, and even if I were to turn out like that

counterexamples.description: Saber’s proposed intervention and unfinished recognition survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber offers to stop Archer, but Shirou interrupts and she cannot finish “Archer is your—”.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber’s proposed intervention and unfinished recognition survive.

contexts.japanese: アーチャーは、貴方の
contexts.english: Archer is your...

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s belief that he knew Archer remains qualified.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He now thinks he probably understood from their first meeting, while describing the reaction then as reasonless repulsion.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s belief that he knew Archer remains qualified.

contexts.japanese: 多分、出会った時から解ってた
contexts.english: I think I knew who he was from the first time I met him.

counterexamples.description: Arm sensation and total fighting strength remain separate measures.
counterexamples.sourceReading: About half the arm sensation remains, while total power is under one tenth and independent action is near its limit.
counterexamples.explanation: Arm sensation and total fighting strength remain separate measures.

contexts.japanese: 残された力は、もはや元の一割にも満たない。
contexts.english: remaining strength is less than a tenth of his original powers.

counterexamples.description: The initially “granted” wish is immediately corrected to almost granted.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration first says the wish came true, then corrects itself: one final push remains.
counterexamples.explanation: The initially “granted” wish is immediately corrected to almost granted.

contexts.japanese: いや、あと一押しで叶おうとしている。
contexts.english: No, it is about to be granted.

counterexamples.description: Eternity and an instant remain equivalent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: For Archer, eternity is an instant and an instant eternity, preventing him from measuring how long he waited.
counterexamples.explanation: Eternity and an instant remain equivalent.

contexts.japanese: 永遠は一瞬であり、一瞬は永遠なのだ。
contexts.english: An eternity is an instant, and an instant is an eternity.

counterexamples.description: Archer’s death threat remains directed at Gilgamesh.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer tells the named Gilgamesh that he will die here if he will not accept the delay.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer’s death threat remains directed at Gilgamesh.

contexts.japanese: ここで死ぬ事になるぞギルガメッシュ
contexts.english: you will die here, Gilgamesh.

counterexamples.description: The no-harm term remains an agreement with Shirou, not a magical Master contract.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer names an agreement with Shirou, its dawn limit, and what happens afterward.
counterexamples.explanation: The no-harm term remains an agreement with Shirou, not a magical Master contract.

contexts.japanese: 傷をつけるな、というのが衛宮士郎との契約だ
contexts.english: The agreement with Shirou Emiya was that she will not be harmed

counterexamples.description: The English preserves the single-pendant deduction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou realizes there cannot be two pendants.
counterexamples.explanation: The English preserves the single-pendant deduction.

contexts.japanese: あのペンダントが二つある筈がない。
contexts.english: there can't be two pendants.

counterexamples.description: The literal and figurative killing sequence is preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer says he killed people, killed hopes, saved only visible objects, and killed still more wishes.
counterexamples.explanation: The literal and figurative killing sequence is preserved.

contexts.japanese: 何十という人間の救いを殺して、目に見えるモノだけの救いを生かして、より多くの願いを殺してきた。
contexts.english: I killed the hopes of dozens of people, saved those whom I could see, and killed the wishes of even more.

counterexamples.description: Archer's probable self-directed rage remains qualified.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou judges that the rising angry shout is probably directed only at Archer himself.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's probable self-directed rage remains qualified.

contexts.japanese: こみ上げる怒声は、おそらく自身に対してのみ。
contexts.english: The rage in his voice is probably directed at himself.

counterexamples.description: Archer's erasure theory remains uncertain.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He argues only that there is a possibility a sufficiently large self-caused paradox might erase Emiya.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's erasure theory remains uncertain.

contexts.japanese: それが自身の手によるモノならば矛盾は大きくなる。
contexts.english: if I do it myself, the paradox might become too large.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's final question about regret is direct and intact.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Before crossing the point of no return, Shirou asks whether Archer regrets his path.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's final question about regret is direct and intact.

contexts.japanese: アーチャー。おまえ、後悔してるのか
contexts.english: Archer. Do you regret it?

counterexamples.description: The duel as a contest in making swords is preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer says fighting him means competing in 剣製, the production of swords.
counterexamples.explanation: The duel as a contest in making swords is preserved.

contexts.japanese: オレと戦うという事は、剣製を競い合うという事だと
contexts.english: A battle with me means a sword-making competition.

counterexamples.description: The headache is correctly distinguished from Projection load.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou identifies it as the recurring symptom associated with approaching Archer.
counterexamples.explanation: The headache is correctly distinguished from Projection load.

contexts.japanese: 即座に行った投影魔術の負荷じゃない。
contexts.english: It isn't from the burden of the Projection.

counterexamples.description: Archer's technique remains optimized for Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The method was developed over years into the combat form best suited to Emiya Shirou.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's technique remains optimized for Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮士郎にとって最適の戦闘方法
contexts.english: the most optimal combat techniques for Shirou Emiya

counterexamples.description: The repeated refusal of pity and impending self-recognition are preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou repeats that he does not pity Archer, yet imagining his own feet walking that path nearly breaks him.
counterexamples.explanation: The repeated refusal of pity and impending self-recognition are preserved.

contexts.japanese: 同情なんてしない、けれど。
contexts.english: Don't feel sorry for him...but...

counterexamples.description: The previous-life possession magic remains an analogy, not a ritual being performed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer says he has heard of such Evocation and compares it to Shirou gaining skill through exchanges.
counterexamples.explanation: The previous-life possession magic remains an analogy, not a ritual being performed.

contexts.japanese: 前世の自分を降霊、憑依させる事で、かつての技術を修得する魔術があると聞く
contexts.english: I've heard of Evocations where the user is possessed by a previous life to learn their past skills

counterexamples.description: Archer's uncertainty about the failed defense remains uncertainty.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He is genuinely puzzled that he could not handle a blow that should have been easy to stop.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's uncertainty about the failed defense remains uncertainty.

contexts.japanese: 捌けなかった事が、本当に不思議だった。
contexts.english: Truly, he wonders why he didn't defend against an attack that would have been easy to stop.

counterexamples.description: Archer's lowered arms preserve acceptance of defeat without declaring death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Though capable of counterattack, he leaves both hands down and unmoving; Shirou understands the meaning.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's lowered arms preserve acceptance of defeat without declaring death.

contexts.japanese: ヤツの両手は下げられたまま動く気配がない。
contexts.english: his arms remain at his sides, and show no sign of movement.

counterexamples.description: Archer's second rescue is retained separately.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Still impaled, he runs to Shirou and shoves him away again during the larger barrage.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's second rescue is retained separately.

contexts.japanese: ヤツは串刺しにされたままで俺へと走り寄り、もう一度突き飛ばした。
contexts.english: He runs toward me looking like a pincushion, and gives me another shove.

counterexamples.description: Rin’s unnamed comparison remains unnamed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She says Shirou is astonishingly similar to another person without identifying that person here.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin’s unnamed comparison remains unnamed.

contexts.japanese: まさかここまで一緒とは思わなかった！
contexts.english: I didn't think you were this similar!

counterexamples.description: The shooter becoming the target word reversal remains functional.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin jokes that Archer, one who hits targets, cannot himself be made an easy target.
counterexamples.explanation: The shooter becoming the target word reversal remains functional.

contexts.japanese: 的を射るアイツが的にされてちゃしょうがない
contexts.english: He can't be the target when he's the one who should be shooting.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s imitation extends from Archer’s swords and technique to his breathing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The increasing bodily depth of imitation remains explicit.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s imitation extends from Archer’s swords and technique to his breathing.

contexts.japanese: 今、息遣いさえも真似ている。
contexts.english: and now even his breathing.

counterexamples.description: Archer’s “Drown in your ideals” formulation is repeated consistently.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The exact phrase remains lodged in Shirou’s mind and frames the confrontation.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer’s “Drown in your ideals” formulation is repeated consistently.

contexts.japanese: 理想を抱いて溺死しろ
contexts.english: Drown in your ideals.

counterexamples.description: Shirou stops Archer because he needs to understand the motive behind attempted murder followed by help.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The contradiction driving the confrontation remains personal and unresolved.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou stops Archer because he needs to understand the motive behind attempted murder followed by help.

contexts.japanese: 俺を殺そうとし、今ここで手助けをするこいつの真意
contexts.english: his true intention of helping me now, after trying to kill me before

counterexamples.description: The dream retains its third-person final observer.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The graveyard comparison belongs to “he,” and the dream’s ownership is not named.
counterexamples.explanation: The dream retains its third-person final observer.

contexts.japanese: 彼は思った。
contexts.english: He thinks that

counterexamples.description: The unusual sword count retains both numerical bounds and subjective uncountability.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The count exceeds ten or twenty, remains below one or two hundred, yet may as well be unlimited to a human unable to count it.
counterexamples.explanation: The unusual sword count retains both numerical bounds and subjective uncountability.

contexts.japanese: 人に数えきれぬのであらば、それは無限と呼ばれるだろう。
contexts.english: if someone can't count them all, the total number may as well be unlimited.

counterexamples.description: Rin recognizes the attack’s bomb principle.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her partial technical understanding is preserved separately from the weapon’s identity.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin recognizes the attack’s bomb principle.

contexts.japanese: アレはただの爆弾だ
contexts.english: It was just a bomb.

counterexamples.description: Repairing a destroyed Noble Phantasm remains difficult.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The translation does not make repair easy or automatic.
counterexamples.explanation: Repairing a destroyed Noble Phantasm remains difficult.

contexts.japanese: 破壊された宝具の修復は容易い事ではない
contexts.english: It is not easy to fix a Noble Phantasm that has been destroyed.

counterexamples.description: Archer’s magecraft is not presently Shirou’s safe capability.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Future appropriation remains only possible now, and projection would collapse him internally.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer’s magecraft is not presently Shirou’s safe capability.

contexts.japanese: 今はまだ可能性があるだけ
contexts.english: it's only a possibility for now.

counterexamples.description: Recognition comes hazily through the firing-hammer image.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The operating-table vision is recalled with dream ruby and partial understanding.
counterexamples.explanation: Recognition comes hazily through the firing-hammer image.

contexts.japanese: 漠然と頭の中に入ってくる
contexts.english: A hazy understanding

counterexamples.description: The arm’s usefulness and his survivability are unknown.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He sees a weapon but asks whether effective/masterable/endurable.
counterexamples.explanation: The arm’s usefulness and his survivability are unknown.

contexts.japanese: 何処まで通じるかは判らない
contexts.english: I don't know how well it'll work

counterexamples.description: His opening weapon confidence reverses to no weapon.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Lost own arm cannot be relied on; alien must suppressed and taints through life.
counterexamples.explanation: His opening weapon confidence reverses to no weapon.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮士郎に武器などない
contexts.english: Shirou Emiya has no weapon.

counterexamples.description: Latent Noble Phantasm knowledge starts with graft.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Illya says he already knew, though next answer tentative.
counterexamples.explanation: Latent Noble Phantasm knowledge starts with graft.

contexts.japanese: 移植された時から知ってる
contexts.english: known ever since his arm was grafted onto you.

counterexamples.description: Weapon-copying Projection answer stays tentative.
counterexamples.sourceReading: I-think/right preserve uncertainty.
counterexamples.explanation: Weapon-copying Projection answer stays tentative.

contexts.japanese: 本当だと思う
contexts.english: I think so.

counterexamples.description: Illya alone knows the special relation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin knows ordinary transplant pain, not what this specific relation will cause.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya alone knows the special relation.

contexts.japanese: シロウとアーチャーの関係
contexts.english: your relationship to Archer.

counterexamples.description: Ownership based on Archer’s arm remains possessive rhetoric.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Life saved by her Archer and continued acceptance motivate my-life/my-Archer claims.
counterexamples.explanation: Ownership based on Archer’s arm remains possessive rhetoric.

contexts.japanese: あいつはわたしのアーチャーなの
contexts.english: he's my Archer.

counterexamples.description: Shirou is surprised Illya knows Archer’s inner-image nature.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Question how she knows, not actual formal ability name reveal.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou is surprised Illya knows Archer’s inner-image nature.

contexts.japanese: アーチャーの魔術が
contexts.english: Archer's magecraft

counterexamples.description: Even one actual arm use threatens loss of self.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Not just temporary earlier memory impairment, cannot remain Shirou.
counterexamples.explanation: Even one actual arm use threatens loss of self.
